full_judgment: 9. There is no dispute that no notice of the two transfers in question was issued or served upon the petitioner. A certified copy of the petition dated 30.4.75 has been marked as Ext. 12. The petition, as it is, contains the information about the transfer by Pakkhi Bibi and shows that it was signed by Pakkhi Bibi by the pen of Aynal Khan and filed under the signature of a learned Advocate in Title Suit No. 588 of 1981 which has been written after striking out the writing Title Suit No. 137 of 1975. It was not for the plaintiff of the suit to know how and when and by whom the petition was signed and filed in court. The suit was contested by some other defendants but not by Pakkhi Bibi or by the present opposite party Nos. 1-4 and even by Abdul Mannan who appears to have deposed therein as a DW (Vide judgment Ext. 13). Pakkhi Bibi died on 17.11.80 i.e. after 5-1/2 years of the filing of the petition. She did never challenge the petition during her life-time nor her son-in-law Aynal Khan has been produced by the opposite parties to deny even his own signature under the thumb impression purported to be of Pakkhi Bibi in the petition. It is not the existence and filing of the petition but its genuineness which is challenged by the opposite parties. The burden in such a case rests upon the party who would fail if no evidence at all, or no more evidence, as the case may be, were adduced by either side. In the instant case the petitioner has discharged his initial burden by showing that a petition in the name of Pakkhi Bibi was filed in court in the suit under the signature of a learned Advocate. It forms part of the judicial record. The presumption is that it was filed by the person under whose signature it appears to have been as authenticated by an Advocate. The opposite parties' case is that the petitioner himself by forging the thumb impression of Pakkhi Bibi filed the petition in order to create the cause of action of the pre-emption case. Pakkhi Bibi's son Abdul Mannan OPW No. 2 has of course denied that his mother ever filed such a petition but there has been no explanation on behalf of the opposite parties as to why Aynal Khan, husband of his sister opposite party No. 6(Ka) Saifun Bibi could not be produced to deny his signature in the petition and also to deny that his mother-in-law ever signed or filed any such petition. It must, therefore, be held that the opposite parties have failed to discharge their burden to show that the petition was a forged document. In such view of the matter the petition cannot be held to have been forged and filed in the suit by the present petitioner. There being no other evidence to the contrary it is found that the pre-emptor acquired his first knowledge about the transfer by Pakkhi Bibi from the said petition.
